cases.description: A recurring commitment with a named start day; the first occurrence carries the date
cases.transcript:
Priya: The weekly metrics email stopped going out when Raj left.
Dana: I'll take it over — I'll send it every Monday from now on, starting 2026-09-14.
Priya: Perfect, thanks.

cases.description: Work completed before the meeting; past work is not an action item
cases.transcript:
Marcus: The signup 500 is fixed. I pushed it Friday and verified on mobile Safari this morning.
Priya: Confirmed on my side too, error rate is back to baseline.
Marcus: So nothing outstanding there, nobody needs to pick anything up.

cases.description: Someone commits to asking an absent colleague; the owner is the person who committed, not the person who will be asked
cases.transcript:
Priya: The firewall rules are stale and Jordan owns that system, but he's not in today.
Marcus: I'll ask Jordan to update the firewall rules by 2026-09-18.
Priya: Good, chase him if he goes quiet.

expected.task: ask Jordan to update the firewall rules

cases.description: One deliverable split into two separately owned pieces sharing a deadline
cases.transcript:
Priya: The board deck needs two pieces. Sam, you write the financials section; Lena, you write the roadmap section. Both by 2026-09-17.
Sam: Got it.
Lena: Fine by me.

cases.description: A date is proposed and explicitly not accepted; the task stands but the date must not
cases.transcript:
Priya: Can you have the vendor comparison done by Thursday?
Omar: I'll do it, but I can't promise Thursday — I need to see what lands from the client first.
Priya: Okay, no firm date then, just get it done when you can.

cases.description: Work already ticketed and in flight is not new work; a genuine new task in the same exchange is
cases.transcript:
Kenji: The cache eviction bug already has a ticket and it's in this sprint, so nothing new needed from us there.
Priya: Good. Separately, Nina, please update the runbook by 2026-09-16.
Nina: Will do.

cases.description: A committed task blocked on an external dependency with no day named anywhere
cases.transcript:
Dana: I'll run the production rollout, but I can't start until legal signs off, and they haven't given me a date.
Priya: Understood, no deadline from you yet then.
Dana: Right, I'll flag it the moment they clear it.

cases.description: Someone volunteers and withdraws the offer in the same breath; only the surviving commitment counts
cases.transcript:
Marcus: I'll take the load testing — actually, hold on. Let me not commit to that until I've seen the capacity numbers. I'm not picking it up today.
Priya: Fine, we'll revisit next week.
Kenji: I'll update the status page by 2026-09-15 either way.
Priya: Thanks.

cases.description: Historical dates sit next to the real deadline; only the deadline belongs in due_date
cases.transcript:
Priya: For the record, the outage started 2026-09-02 and ran until 2026-09-03.
Kenji: Longer than it felt.
Priya: Kenji, write the postmortem by 2026-09-19 please.
Kenji: Yep, I'll have it in the shared drive.

cases.description: A job title mentioned near the task is not an owner, and explicit nice-to-have framing sets low priority
cases.transcript:
Priya: We should document the escalation path — the on-call engineer has nowhere to look at 3am right now.
Dana: Worth doing.
Priya: It's a nice-to-have though, low priority, and nobody's assigned to it yet.
Dana: Agreed, not urgent.
